findings.title: Opening a figure's details and then switching Figures or View destroys the drawer and stops every figure from opening
findings.evidence: Script claims/../repro_drawer.js on the committed build: click .fig[data-id=ronnie_coleman] → drawer open: true. Click #hReal → 'after Real heights: drawer exists: false', pageerror "TypeError: Failed to execute 'appendChild' on 'Node': parameter 1 is not of type 'Node'." Clicking Phil Heath afterwards throws the same error again and no drawer opens. Cause: placeDrawer moves #drawer inside a .stop section. renderStops then clears #stops with innerHTML='', which deletes the drawer element. placeDrawer then calls sec.appendChild(null). The same happens for Side/Front. test/shots.js sweeps the controls but never with a drawer open.
findings.expected: Switching mode with a drawer open should redraw the figures and keep the drawer (or close it) without errors.
findings.fix: At the start of renderStops, move the drawer back to document.body (document.body.appendChild($('drawer'))) before clearing #stops. Or create the drawer outside #stops and only position it. Add a shots.js step: open a drawer, toggle Real heights and Side, and assert there are no page errors and a figure still opens.

findings.title: data/limits.json is stale: the page shows the Vasen 'softer line' the verifier rejected, and no test catches the drift
findings.location: data/limits.json notes[2] (generated by tools/compute_limits.js from data/settings.json limits.notes[2], line 720); rendered in #limitsNotes
findings.evidence: node compare: settings has 'A softer line comes earlier. Unaided eating and drinking use about 130 to 136° of elbow bend; with the elbow held to 120°, 49 of 50 people still managed ... (Vasen 1995), the lowest setting tested.' limits.json and the rendered page have 'A softer line comes earlier: with the elbow held to 120°, people still manage eating, drinking and washing by moving the shoulder and wrist instead (Vasen 1995).' The verifier (research/round1/verify_function.json rec_vasen_120_line) said this exact wording is mislabelled: the earlier line is ~130-136°, and 120° is only the lowest brace setting tested, with 49 of 50 succeeding. As rendered, the 'softer line' is never named, and 'people still manage' turns 49 of 50 into everyone. test.js checks that outline.json and duo-outlines.json match their tools, but has no such check for limits.json.
findings.expected: The page shows the corrected settings text, and generated limits.json always matches settings.json.
findings.fix: Re-run node tools/compute_limits.js and rebuild. Add a test that limits.json verdict, method, notes and each item's label, short and definition equal settings.limits. A full recompute is slow, so compare the text only.

findings.title: 'Rex and Ollie are past the first two limits' is inferred from A-pose art, where the arms are out by design
findings.location: data/settings.json stops[duo].sub (line 760) and limits.notes[3] (line 721); rendered in the Rex and Ollie stop and the limits notes
findings.evidence: Page: 'Their art shows arms held out and thighs touching: by the drawn body's own limits, they are past the first two.' and 'their art shows their arms well out ... so they are past the first two limits whatever their score.' The turnarounds are A-pose sheets. BRIEF.md line 78 specifies 'A-pose, arms about 30–40° out', and line 63 records 'The arms clear the torso in the front views', so the art shows daylight between arm and torso. The arms limit is defined as 'Held as close as the outlines allow, the arms stand at least 30° out'. No code tests this on the traced duo outlines: compute_limits.js runs only human templates, and Figure.armRestAngle needs a re-posable template. In duo.jpg Ollie has his hands on his hips. Posed-out arms do not show that the arms cannot hang down.
findings.expected: Claims about the duo's limits should be tested on their outlines or stated as untested. Thigh contact can be described as visible in the art.
findings.fix: Reword to: 'Their thighs touch in the art. Their arms are posed out (A-pose), so the art can't show whether they could hang down; Step 2 can test that on the new sheets.' Make the same change in limits.notes[3].

findings.title: 'Largest fat-free mass measured: a sumo wrestler' (121.3 kg) is contradicted by builds on the same page
findings.location: data/settings.json anchors.natural[sumo].label (line 608); forest anchor row and natural-limit card; stops[top].sub
findings.evidence: Forest and card: 'Largest fat-free mass measured: a sumo wrestler · 34 · MEASURED' (121.3 kg FFM). The Kraemer 2020 build on the same page is a DXA group mean of 18 strongmen. builds.json kraemer2020_elite_strongmen_dxa gives lean_mass_kg 118 + BMC_kg 5.23 = 123.2 kg, and its drawer shows '1.8 × 124 kg ÷ 1.87³'. A group mean above 121.3 kg means some individuals were larger (lean SD 11.7). Brian Shaw's drawer shows 144 kg FFM (brian_shaw_height_weight FFM_Feb2024_derived_kg 143.8, from a reported hydrostatic test). The stop text is hedged ('found in a study of its upper limit'), but the anchor label is not.
findings.expected: The label should not claim a record the page's own data beats.
findings.fix: Relabel as 'Kondo 1994's largest sumo wrestler: 121 kg fat-free mass' (kind: measured individual). Drop 'largest' or say 'largest in a study of the upper limit'.

findings.title: Comic giants stop says 'Their heights and weights are official', but Hulk (grey) is fan-wiki only
findings.evidence: Rendered: 'Their heights and weights are official.' The band includes Hulk (grey), at 83 the second-highest giant. His drawer shows 'Fan-wiki figures only (reported)', 'HEIGHT COUNTED 1.98 m REPORTED 6'6" (fan wiki only)' and 'WEIGHT COUNTED 408 kg (900 lb) REPORTED 900 lb (fan wiki only)'. data.json: hulk_grey Hst 'reported', Wst 'reported'. He also helps set the band's span ('score 69 to 84').
findings.expected: The stop copy should match each member's status: fan-site numbers are labelled as such.
findings.fix: Build the sentence from the members' statuses, e.g. 'Their heights and weights are official, except the grey Hulk's (fan wiki only).' Or flag hulk_grey on its plate.

findings.title: Brian Shaw carries a DERIVED chip although his body fat is only reported, and the key says DERIVED means 'body fat measured'
findings.location: src/app.html scoreStatus (lines 586-590); key text 'DERIVED: body fat measured' and forest sub 'unless it carries a DERIVED chip (body fat measured)'
findings.evidence: builds.json brian_shaw.body_fat_pct = {value 17.6, status 'reported', method 'hydrostatic weighing, self-filmed test relayed by FitnessVolt (Feb 2024)'}. scoreStatus returns 'derived' whenever no input is 'estimate' or 'unknown', so 'reported' passes. Rendered: the Brian Shaw plate shows '30–34 · 32 at 18% fat · DERIVED', and the forest row shows 'Brian Shaw 30–34 DERIVED'. The drawer's own body-fat row says REPORTED. status_vocabulary defines reported as 'not independently measured'.
findings.expected: Per the page's key, DERIVED only where body fat is measured. A reported body fat should not lift the chip.
findings.fix: In scoreStatus, require bodyFat.status === 'measured' for 'derived' (treat 'reported' as estimate). Or add a REPORTED tier and reword the key and the forest sub.

findings.title: Masthead cluster 'Every real man 13–42' starts at Bruce Banner, a comic character
findings.location: src/app.html drawGlance (line 1131: lowest = LIST.reduce over every build)
findings.evidence: Rendered at 1280 px: 'EVERY REAL MAN 13–42'; at 390 px: 'REAL MEN 13–42'. lowest = min score.lo over LIST = 12.82, which is bruce_banner (Comic characters). The lowest real man's range bottom is ansur2_m_p95 at 18.66 (data.json). So real men's ranges run 19–42, or 20–39 at working values.
findings.expected: 'Every real man 19–42'.
findings.fix: Compute lowest over HUMANS (LIST.filter(isHuman)), not LIST.

findings.title: 'These studies did no testing of their own' is unsupported for Currier 2019; the verifier's correction was never applied
findings.evidence: Page: 'The NCAA tests at random, but these studies did no testing of their own' (Trexler and Currier) and 'The footballer studies did no drug tests of their own'. facts.json currier2019_ffmi_check verify: 'Drug testing is unknown, not 'none'. The recommendation's 'these studies did no testing' is unsupported for Currier', corrected: 'drug testing: not stated in abstract (unknown)'. verify_natural.json item 6 says the same. research/corrections.json has no entry for it. Currier is also ten sports, not footballers.
findings.expected: Only Trexler is stated to have done no independent testing; Currier's testing is unknown.
findings.fix: 'Trexler's study did no drug testing of its own (NCAA tests at random); Currier's abstract does not say.' Change the past25 sub to match.

findings.title: Kouri non-user labels overstate who the 74 were and contradict the 'under 25' text
findings.location: data/settings.json anchors.natural[kouri].label (line 544), builds[kouri1995_nonusers].short (line 201); builds.json kouri1995_nonusers description, height and weight basis
findings.evidence: (a) Forest label 'Kouri 1995: highest of 74 drug-free lifters ... 25' and plate 'Kouri's drug-free lifters'. The drawer says '74 male gym athletes'. facts kouri1995_fulltext_methods: testosterone_study_nonusers 18, i.e. 18 of the 74 came from a testosterone trial, not gyms (verify_natural.json: 'The 74 drug-free lifters label should reflect both'). (b) 'highest ... 25' sits beside text saying all 74 'scored under 25'. kouri1995_fig2_distribution: top non-user bin 24.0–24.9, exact top not printed. (c) The drawer says 'Means come second-hand from Helms and McDonald' with REPORTED 'secondary source' height and weight. The full text (Table 1: 1.80 m, 82.06 kg) was read and verified in kouri1995_fulltext_methods.
findings.expected: Labels that match the paper: 74 non-users (56 gym athletes, 18 trial volunteers), all under 25; primary-source means.
findings.fix: Label: 'Kouri 1995: 74 non-users all under 25 (height-normalised FFMI)'; short: 'Kouri's non-users'. Update the builds.json description and basis to cite Table 1 (claim builds.json in STATUS.md first).

findings.title: 'The heaviest comic characters' is wrong: the band and the lede are the highest-scoring, not the heaviest
findings.evidence: Lede: 'the heaviest comic characters about 84' (Abomination, 444.5 kg). Darkseid (823 kg), Hulk Marvel.com (522 kg) and Hulk savage (472 kg) are heavier. Stop: 'The heaviest comic characters score 69 to 84'. Doomsday at 415 kg is heavier than Juggernaut (408 kg) and Hulk grey (408 kg), yet he scores 34 and sits in the 32–42 band.
findings.expected: Wording that matches the selection (highest score).
findings.fix: 'the most heavily built comic characters' or 'the top comic characters'.

findings.title: Mr America anchor: 'Only the guessed body fat and that weight differ' is contradicted by the verifier
findings.evidence: The page says Kouri's and Todd's estimates differ only in fat guesses and Grimek's weight. facts kouri1995_mr_america_table2 verify: 'It uses Todd's heights and weights, which are not Kouri's inputs ... Kouri's Willoughby weights differ, at least for Grimek'. The builds_json_kouri_corrections verify adds 'The input weights differ for some rows as well as the fat' (e.g. Reeves 213 lb program vs Todd 192 lb). The '25.8 on this scale with their heights' conversion also uses Todd's heights, not Kouri's.
findings.expected: Kouri used Willoughby 1970's heights and weights; Todd used her own; inputs differ for several men.
findings.fix: Replace the last sentence with: 'The two used different height and weight records (Kouri: Willoughby 1970) and different fat guesses; the conversions to this scale use Todd's heights.'

findings.title: Score card says Kouri's correction was 'fitted to men of 1.55 to 2.05 m'; that range is the Build Calculator's own window
findings.evidence: Rendered: 'at Rex's height Kouri's correction, fitted to men of 1.55 to 2.05 m, would give about 250 instead of 160.' 1.55–2.05 is calc.js FFMI_NORM_RANGE (line 41), where the calculator chooses to apply Kouri. Kouri fitted the slope on 'elite nonusers with FFMI ≥ 22' (kouri1995_fulltext_methods). The sample's extremes were the 1.59 m shortest non-user and 'one of the tallest' at 1.93 m.
findings.expected: 'fitted to human athletes (about 1.6 to 1.9 m)'.
findings.fix: Change the clause to 'fitted to drug-free athletes of about 1.6 to 1.9 m'. If wanted, mention that the calculator applies it only from 1.55 to 2.05 m.

findings.title: 'A few measured athletes do' reach 25: in Trexler it was more than a quarter
findings.evidence: Rendered: 'No drug-free man in Kouri's study reached 25 on his scale. A few measured athletes do: the top 2.5% of college footballers start at 28...' facts trexler2017_ffmi_fulltext_check: n_over_25 = 62 of 235 (26.4%).
findings.expected: 'Many measured athletes do: 62 of 235 college footballers (26%) were above 25; the top 2.5% start at 28 ...'
findings.fix: Replace 'A few' with the count.

findings.title: Bruce Banner's body-fat range is called 'the range of measured US soldiers', but it comes from the tape equation
findings.location: data/settings.json fat_classes.comic_everyday.note (line 104); drawer and fat card
findings.evidence: Drawer: 'Assumed: the range of measured US soldiers.' 15–34% is the official one-site equation's P5–P95 on ANSUR II (ansur2_men_bodyfat_from_army_equation: p5 15.2, p95 33.5, status 'estimate'). ANSUR II has no measured body fat. Taylor's equation gives 17.3–36.5.
findings.expected: 'the range estimated for US soldiers from waist and weight'.
findings.fix: Reword the note. Optionally widen to cover both equations, as the soldiers' own ranges do.

findings.title: Drawer 'What this ignores' lines are wrong for Rex, Ollie and the soldiers
findings.evidence: Rex and Ollie drawers: 'Beyond human data: no real man scores this high, so his shape and body fat are extrapolated.' Their shapes are traced from their turnarounds, and their 5–10% body fat is the owner's canon (bodyfat_range_rex_ollie, status official). Rex, Ollie and every ANSUR soldier also get 'Body fat is assumed for his group.' The soldiers' fat is estimated from each build's own waist and weight, as their body-fat row says.
findings.expected: Lines that match each build's basis.
findings.fix: Duo: 'Beyond human data: no real man scores this high.' Body-fat line by kind: army_equation → 'Body fat is estimated from his waist and weight'; duo → 'Body fat is the owner's canon range'; class → keep.

findings.title: Rounding rules broken: '220–920' for the stretch to 924, and a tool score shown as '101.4'
findings.evidence: Close-up forest (Close-up, 12 to 45): 'EMPTY · 220 TO 924 | off this scale: 220–920 →'. off() runs scr() on MEAT, which rounds 924.1 to two significant figures. Target tool: 'it measures 101.4 (target 100)'. The rules are 924 exact and two significant figures from 100.
findings.expected: 'off this scale: 220–924 →' and 'it measures 100 (target 100)'.
findings.fix: In off(), print MEAT_TXT when hi is MEAT (e.g. hi >= MEAT - 1e-6). In drawTarget, use sc(s) for the measured score.

findings.title: 'No builds here' and 'Hatched: nothing there' are shown where Thor and the Thing sit
findings.evidence: Gap tile for 42–62 (claims/gap1.png): 'NO BUILDS HERE' printed in the same tile as the markers 'THE THING · 59' and 'THOR · 62', above 'On their listed weights, inside this stretch:' with both figures. Glance tape: the hatch spans x 350.5–461.2 px, and the Thing tick sits at 444.1 and Thor at 458.2 (claims/glance.js). The caption reads 'Hatched: nothing there.'
findings.expected: 'Nothing comparable here' when a stretch holds flagged builds.
findings.fix: Use 'Nothing comparable here' when item.inside.length > 0. Change the caption to 'Hatched: nothing comparable there.'

findings.title: Last stretch says the hands-to-face band lies 'across this stretch and beyond', but it covers only its first few percent
findings.evidence: Stop 'Score 220 to 924': 'The hands to face limit lies somewhere from 86 to 230, across this stretch and beyond'. The band is 86.06–233.31 and the stretch 216.2–924.1, so the band overlaps only 216–233. The condition (range[0] < g.from) is true because the band extends below the stretch, not across it.
findings.expected: 'from 86 to 230; it reaches only the bottom of this stretch'.
findings.fix: Branch: if range[0] < g.from && range[1] > g.to → 'across this stretch and beyond'; if only range[0] < g.from → 'reaching into the bottom of this stretch'; if only range[1] > g.to → 'from inside this stretch upward'.

findings.title: The Thing: drawer says 'his score is too high' as fact; no source says the hide is denser or heavier
findings.evidence: Drawer: 'Marvel describes his skin as a rock-like hide. No source says how much of his weight it is, so his score is too high by an unknown amount.' facts thing_rocky_hide: hide_mass_kg null, hide_density_kg_m3 null; Marvel calls the skin 'supple'; density claims are fan-wiki only. His plate and forest rows say 'may be overstated'.
findings.expected: Hedged wording like the plate's.
findings.fix: '... so his score may be too high, by an amount no source gives.'

findings.title: MEASURED chips on anchor values that are converted to this scale
findings.location: data/settings.json anchors.natural[sumo] and [tail] (status 'measured'); forest anchor rows and the stops[top] chip
findings.evidence: Sumo row: '34 MEASURED'. 33.9 is S computed from the measured FFM and height (1.8×121.3/1.86³). The top stop puts '{chip:measured}' after 'scores 34'. Athletes row '28–29 MEASURED': the range [28.0, 28.7] is currier p97_5_all_S_at_mean_height_approx 28 and rugby 28.7 ('approx' S conversions). It is mixed with Trexler's unconverted 28.1, whose conversion at the mean height is 27.5 (trexler p97_5_S_at_mean_height), outside the range.
findings.expected: DERIVED for converted values, with one conversion rule per anchor.
findings.fix: Set status 'derived' (or show 'measured, converted') for sumo and the athletes' range. Use either all source values (28.1–29.1) or all conversions (27.5–28.7).

findings.title: The same lean median-soldier shape scores 27 in the limits section and 26 in the measuring tool
findings.location: src/app.html renderLimits first card (limits.json templates[0].score_at_f1 = 26.98) vs exampleSheet/measure (armDeg 35, figurePx 700)
findings.evidence: Limit card: '27 · The median soldier's own shape · Scored lean (7.5% fat) ...'. Tool status: 'The example is the median soldier at 1.80 m, counted at 7.5% fat and 1,060 kg/m³ like Rex and Ollie' with results 'Mass 90 kg', 'Score 26 (24–28)'. 90 kg gives S 25.7, against 26.98: a 5% gap for one described shape.
findings.expected: One number for one stated shape, or the difference explained.
findings.fix: Render the tool example with the same arm angle and resolution compute_limits uses (or vice versa), or note that the arm angle and resolution move the reading by a few percent.

findings.title: Withers drawer shows a height range of '1.78–1.78 m'
findings.evidence: Withers 1997 drawer: 'The range covers body fat 3–7% and height 1.78–1.78 m.' builds.json height range [1.776, 1.783] rounds to the same value at both ends.
findings.expected: Omit the height clause when both ends round alike, or show 3 decimals.
findings.fix: Compare the formatted strings, and push the height range only if they differ.

findings.title: Rex's tail is 307 kg, but its stated basis gives 306 kg
findings.evidence: Drawer: '2,700 kg less 307 kg of tail' with 'tail 0.289 m^3 at 1,060 kg/m^3'. 0.289 × 1,060 = 306.3. builds.json rex_ollie_picture_mass segments_m3.rex.tail = 0.289, and the index verifier computed 306 kg (facts same_shape_scaled_to_3048 verify).
findings.expected: 306 kg, or a volume that gives 307 (0.290 m³).
findings.fix: Set mass_kg 306 (and test.js 2700 − 306), or cite the unrounded volume.

findings.title: Thigh-limit definition says 'about twice an ordinary step'; the comparison is of step width
findings.evidence: 'From here every step must be at least hip-joint width, about twice an ordinary step.' Source obese_gait_step_width: step width 0.16 vs 0.08 m. Inter-hip-joint 0.174 m (ansur_thigh_gap_legs_vertical). An ordinary step length is about 0.7 m, so read literally the sentence is false.
findings.expected: '... feet at least hip-joint width apart (about 17 cm), about twice an ordinary step width (8 cm).'
findings.fix: Say 'step width' and give the numbers.
